title: Sell Mineral Rights in Westhope, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Westhope, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Westhope, ND close to the Canadian border? Get an honest read on your Bottineau County interest before selling.
heroLead: Westhope sits right at the Canadian border in Bottineau County, about as far from the Bakken core as our coverage area gets, which is precisely why owners here often assume there's nothing to check.
intro: That assumption is usually wrong, or at least incomplete. Bottineau County has decades of conventional oil history layered under it, and Westhope-area families who homesteaded this ground a hundred years ago sometimes still hold mineral rights tied to leases nobody currently remembers signing.

sections.heading: Border-country land with an oil history of its own
paragraphs: Wells near the international border have gone in periodically over the decades targeting shallower formations, and while none of it compares to the scale of Bakken drilling further west, some Westhope tracts do have real production history attached to them. We check the actual record rather than assume based on distance from Williston.

sections.heading: Getting the ownership picture straight first
paragraphs: Because this land has often stayed in the same family since homestead days, it's common for the mineral rights to be owned by several heirs who've never formally divided the interest on paper. Before we make any offer, we confirm exactly who owns what share so the transaction reflects reality, not an outdated deed.

sections.heading: What a fair look at Westhope acreage involves
paragraphs: We start with whatever documentation you have, an old lease, a deed, a tax statement, and use it to pull the Bottineau County Recorder's file directly. From there we check the state's well index for anything drilled, permitted, or currently active near your section.

Only once we've done that research do we tell you honestly what we think your interest is worth, whether that's a real number or a plain acknowledgment that there's little activity to price against right now.

faqs.question: Is it even likely our Westhope minerals have any value this close to the border?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific tract's lease and production history, which we check directly rather than guessing based on location. Some Bottineau County interests near Westhope do carry real value.

faqs.question: We have an old, unsigned lease document. Does that mean we're under lease now?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. An unsigned or expired lease generally doesn't bind you. We'll review whatever documents you have and tell you plainly what your current status is.

faqs.question: Do we need to involve a lawyer to sell our Westhope mineral interest?
faqs.answer: Not usually for a straightforward sale with clear title. We handle the deed and paperwork directly, though you're always welcome to have your own attorney review anything before you sign.

faqs.question: What documentation is most useful to send you first?
faqs.answer: Anything with a legal description, an old lease, deed, or tax statement, gets us started fastest researching your specific tract.
